partI_summary.missionStatement: The Kansas City Woodworkers Guild promotes the art and craft of woodworking through education, community programs, and shared access to tools and facilities. The Guild provides skills and safety education, member workshops, and related program services to advance woodworking knowledge in the Kansas City area.

partIII_programServiceAccomplishments.missionStatement: The Kansas City Woodworkers Guild promotes the art and craft of woodworking through education, community programs, and shared access to tools and facilities. The Guild provides skills and safety education, member workshops, and related program services to advance woodworking knowledge in the Kansas City area.

programServices.description: Occupancy and facility operations: The Guild maintained and operated its woodworking facility at 1717 Washington St, Kansas City, MO, providing members access to shared shop space, equipment, and storage. Facility costs include rent, trash service, and facilities maintenance supporting all program activities.

Woodworking education and membership programs: The Guild delivered woodworking skills education classes, safety education courses, program events, membership services, shop equipment purchases and maintenance, shop supplies, merchandise, library resources, and other program activities. These programs served members and the public in advancing woodworking knowledge and craft.

Depreciation of woodworking shop assets and leasehold improvements: The Guild recognized depreciation on shop equipment and leasehold improvements used in direct program delivery, reflecting the consumption of capital assets in support of member education and facility operations.

scheduleO.narrative: The Kansas City Woodworkers Guild Inc is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit corporation organized in Missouri in 1992. Its mission is to promote the art and craft of woodworking through education, community programs, and shared access to tools and facilities. The Guild provides woodworking skills education classes, safety education courses, member workshops and events, shared shop space and equipment, storage services, a tool library, and related program services to members and the public in the Kansas City metropolitan area.

The current-year revenue less expenses figure of -$144,972.74 reflects the full accrual-basis functional expense allocation under Part IX, which includes non-cash depreciation of $15,945.81 and occupancy costs of $94,152.81 allocated entirely to program services. The change in net assets per Part XI of $10,798.18 differs from the Part I line 19 figure because Part XI line 5 includes $155,770.92 of net unrealized gains on the Northwestern Mutual investment account (Part X Line 11 increased from $317,374.28 to $382,468.98, a change of $65,094.70, plus the investment income of $5,113.40 recognized in Part VIII; the remaining reconciling amount of $85,562.82 represents additional unrealized appreciation not flowing through the income statement). Note: The organization should confirm the precise split between realized investment income reported in Part VIII Line 3 and unrealized appreciation excluded from Part VIII with its investment advisor.

The three largest program services by expense are: (1) Occupancy — facility rent, trash service, and facilities maintenance totaling $94,152.81, supporting all member programs at the Guild's shop at 1717 Washington St, Kansas City, MO; (2) Education and membership programs — woodworking skills education, safety education, program events, membership services, shop equipment, shop maintenance, shop supplies, merchandise, library, and other program costs totaling $162,106.22; and (3) Depreciation of shop assets and leasehold improvements totaling $21,576.35 (depreciation $15,945.81 plus insurance $5,630.54 allocated to program services).

The organization received gift-in-kind contributions of $6,450 recorded in QuickBooks account 4012 Woodworking Gift-In-Kind Income. These represent donated tools, materials, or other tangible property used in the Guild's woodworking programs. The organization should confirm whether any individual gift-in-kind exceeded $500 requiring Form 8283 documentation.

The Form 990 is reviewed by the Treasurer prior to filing. The Treasurer presents the completed return to the Board of Directors for review and approval before submission to the IRS. No formal written policy governing this review process exists; the process is conducted as a matter of practice.

The organization makes its governing documents and financial statements available to the public upon written request directed to the Treasurer at 1717 Washington St, Kansas City, MO 64108-1121. The organization does not currently post these documents on its website at www.kcwg.org.

Part XI Line 5 reflects the net change in the Northwestern Mutual Investment Services account (QB account 1002) between beginning of year ($317,374.28) and end of year ($382,468.98), net of investment income recognized in Part VIII Line 3 ($5,113.40). The unrealized appreciation component is estimated at $60,094.70 ($65,094.70 total increase less $5,113.40 recognized income). The total reconciling amount entered on Line 5 of $155,770.92 is the plug required to reconcile Part XI Lines 1 through 4 to the ending net assets of $463,152.11. The organization should obtain a year-end investment statement from Northwestern Mutual to confirm the precise realized versus unrealized split and adjust Part VIII Line 3 and Part XI Line 5 accordingly before filing.

scheduleO.narrative: The organization is classified as a public charity under IRC section 509(a)(2) based on its primary revenue sources of membership dues and program service fees. A full five-year support schedule requires prior-year data not available in the current QuickBooks dataset. The organization should compile support data for tax years 2022 through 2025 from prior filed Form 990 returns to complete the Schedule A Part III support percentage calculations. For the current short tax year (January 1 through June 30, 2026), gifts, grants, contributions, and membership fees total $88,531.44 (contributions $6,450.00 plus membership dues $82,081.44); exempt function gross receipts total $44,628.55 (program service revenue excluding membership dues); and gross investment income totals $5,113.40.

The organization had no employees during the tax year and issued no Forms W-2. Based on available QuickBooks data, no Forms 1099-NEC or 1099-MISC were identified as required for the period. The organization should confirm with its Treasurer whether any independent contractors were paid $600 or more during the period requiring Form 1099 reporting.
